    The matching quiver of a closed walk #

    Definition 4.5 and Lemma 4.6. The cycle D_w of a closed walk is described by cycle coordinates (CycleCoords): its vertices and arrows are numbered by ZMod r, arrow x joining the vertices x and x + 1, forwards (from x to x + 1) or backwards. For a quiver morphism p : D_w → Q, the matching quiver H has the pairs (j, i) of vertices as vertices, and an edge for each pair of arrows α at j and β at i with the same label, both leaving or both entering (Inc); it joins (j, i) to the pair of the other endpoints (Adj). Components are classes of Conn, the reflexive transitive closure.

    For p injective on the arrows with a fixed source and on those with a fixed target (3.4), we prove the facts of Lemma 4.6 used in Proposition 4.7:

    • diag_iff_of_conn: the diagonal pairs form a union of components;
    • eq_of_conn_of_snd_eq: on each component the second coordinate determines the first;
    • exists_col_not_conn: if the walk is primitive (Primitive: no nontrivial rotation of the cycle preserves the labels and orientations of the arrows), every component off the diagonal misses some second coordinate.

    structure LargeIndecomposable.FinQuiver.CycleCoords (D : FinQuiver) (r : ℕ) :
    Type

    Cycle coordinates on a quiver D: vertices and arrows numbered by ZMod r, the arrow x joining the vertices x and x + 1, from x to x + 1 if fwd holds and from x + 1 to x otherwise.

    • pos : D.V ≃ ZMod r

      The position of a vertex.

    • eix : D.A ≃ ZMod r

      The position of an arrow.

    • fwd : D.A → Bool

      The orientation of an arrow.

    • pos_src (e : D.A) : self.pos (D.src e) = if self.fwd e = true then self.eix e else self.eix e + 1
    • pos_tgt (e : D.A) : self.pos (D.tgt e) = if self.fwd e = true then self.eix e + 1 else self.eix e
